label: rare late-original/delimiter step in long sequences (content-specific, unexplained)
explanation: Very sparse feature (~0.007% of steps). Positionally it is confined to the last original tokens (t=7,8) and the <DEL> step (t=9), almost entirely in L=9 (85% of mass) or L=8 sequences; it essentially never fires in the copy phase (1% mass) or before t=5. The window predicate captures ~92% of activation mass but has ~0.1% precision: within the window only about 1 in 1000 steps fires, so what selects these steps is the sequence content, which I could not isolate. Enriched content: first token o (11.7x), g at positions 1-3, u around positions 4-6, next_out o, and inputs v/m/c/h at the firing step; conjunctions such as orig(0)==o & seen(g) & seen(u) raise precision only to ~9% while dropping recall below 10%. It looks like a sparse code for some hidden-state configuration built from several earlier tokens, not one readable rule. I did not find a clean magnitude modulator; top activations land on the last original token (t=8).

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=o (+3.59), orig1=g (+3.22), orig1=o (+3.01), orig2=g (+2.56), recall_idx=-1 & in_tok=v (+2.55), orig5=u (+2.24). Lower it: phase=2 (-5.59), next_out=- (-3.96), orig8=- (-2.20), orig6=- (-2.18).
